Shalmaneser. The king of Assyria who made Hoshea his servant and besieged Samaria.

WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria; and Hoshea became his servant, and gave him presents." 2 Kings 17:3
When Hoshea sent messengers to So king of Egypt and brought no present "as he had done year by year", "the king of Assyria shut him up, and bound him in prison". 2 Kings 17:4
"Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria, and besieged it. And at the end of three years they took it." 2 Kings 18:9–10
From the textKings does not name the king who took Samaria: 2 Kings 17:6 says "the king of Assyria took Samaria", and 2 Kings 18:10 "they took it". 2 Kings 17:6 2 Kings 18:10
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Kings gives the reason for Samaria's fall: "Because they obeyed not the voice of the LORD their God, but transgressed his covenant". 2 Kings 18:12
Hoshea paid him presents "year by year" until he turned to So king of Egypt. 2 Kings 17:3–4
Samaria endured a three-year siege, and Israel was carried away into Assyria. 2 Kings 17:5–6
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
PROPHETS
The prophets who spoke about him
Ho Hosea “all thy fortresses shall be spoiled, as Shalman spoiled Beth-arbel in the day of battle”
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
LUCKENBILL (1927)
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Scripture gives no year of his own reign; it dates the siege of Samaria to Hoshea's 7th–9th years and Hezekiah's 4th–6th (2 Kgs 18:9–10).
ROGERS (1912)
Tiglath-pileser died in Tebet 727; Shalmaneser V died in 722.
THE BABYLONIAN CHRONICLE
No years given[72][71][75]
"Shalmaneser reigned five years in Akkad and in Assyria." In the same place the Babylonian king list and Ptolemy's canon have a king "Ululai" for five years.
Kings' account
2 Kings 17–18
Kings names Shalmaneser as the king who besieged Samaria and says "at the end of three years they took it", without naming the king who took it. 2 Kings 18:9–10 2 Kings 17:6
Shalmaneser: the chronicle's "Shabarain" is Samaria
A. K. Grayson (1975)
Grayson's edition of the Babylonian Chronicle reads that Shalmaneser ravaged Samaria at the start of his reign. Rogers (1912) printed the name as "Shabarain" without placing it.[2][72]
Sargon, by his own account
Sargon's inscriptions
Sargon lists the capture of Samaria among his deeds "from the year of my accession to the fifteenth year of my reign" (Luckenbill).[34][31]
Shalmaneser's siege, Sargon's claim
R. W. Rogers (1912), following Winckler

Rogers: Samaria fell in 722, immediately on Shalmaneser's death; "Sargon claims the victory for himself, though he could not have been present at all", and the city "may have fallen while Shalmaneser still lived".[80]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 3
2 Kings 17 2 Kings 18 Hosea 10
PASSAGES · 3
2 Kings 17:1–6 2 Kings 18:9–12 Hosea 10:14
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no length for Shalmaneser's reign and does not say how he died.
Kings does not say which king of Assyria was on the throne when Samaria fell.
Scripture does not say what became of Hoshea after he was bound in prison.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
Scholars' viewKings does not number him; historians call him Shalmaneser V, to tell him from earlier kings of the name. 2 Kings 17:3 [21]
From the textThe site's person record for him also holds "Shalman" (Hosea 10:14). Whether Hosea meant this king is a question set out below. Hosea 10:14
